name: Resource Behavior
author: Promenade Team
description: How each person in a log actually works: how much they do, how fast, how specialised, how often they batch or juggle several things at once, and whether they slow down when busy.

actions.label: Resource Behavior
actions.description: Profiles every person in the log: volume, spread of work, collaboration, batching, and — where the log records start and complete separately — service time, waiting time, utilisation, multitasking, and the correlation between how busy someone was and how long their work then took.

agent.whenToUse: Questions about individuals rather than about relations: who carries the volume, who specialises, who is juggling several things at once, who slows down under load. Complements the Social Network plugin, which answers who works with whom.
agent.notFor: A log with no resource attribute or no timestamps — it is not offered there. On a log without lifecycle values every duration metric is reported as unavailable rather than approximated from the gap between events, which would conflate queueing with working.
examples: Profile the resources in this log
Do people here slow down when they have more work in progress?
bucket week to see the workload timeline by week instead of by day
minEvents 50 to drop the occasional visitors

bucket.title: Timeline bucket
bucket.description: Width of one column in the workload timeline. Widened automatically when the log spans more columns than are worth drawing; the effective width is reported.

batchWindowMins.title: Batch window (minutes)
batchWindowMins.description: How close together two identical activities must be to read as one sitting. Batching is a statement about this window, not an absolute property — a shorter one finds fewer, larger runs.

minEvents.title: Minimum events per person
minEvents.description: Drops people below this. A resource seen twice has no meaningful rate, utilisation or correlation, and their rows crowd out the ones that do.

maxResources.title: Resource limit
maxResources.description: Keeps this many people, most active first. The rest are dropped and counted.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Bounds the activity dictionary the scan builds. This log is classified by activity *and* lifecycle phase, so the dictionary is up to three times the number of activities — set it high enough for that.

showScatter.title: Show workload vs speed
showScatter.description: Every work item plotted as how many the person had in progress when it started against how long it then took.

scale.title: Colour scale
scale.description: Linear reads absolute volume; square-root keeps a quiet person visible beside a very busy one.

recommends.reason: the other half of the organisational perspective — who works with whom, rather than how each person works

citation.text: Pika, A., Leyer, M., Wynn, M.T., Fidge, C.J., ter Hofstede, A.H.M., van der Aalst, W.M.P. (2017). Mining Resource Profiles from Event Logs. ACM Transactions on Management Information Systems, 8(1), 1-30.
